"executive_summary": "This paper presents high-speed, multi-wavelength observations of a lunar occultation of the dust-enshrouded carbon star AFGL 5440 (also known as OH 06.86-1.5 and IRAS 18036-2344), obtained on 28 Aug 2001 with the pMIRAS spectrophotometer on the McDonald Observatory 2.7-m telescope. The observations span a continuous wavelength range of 1-4 microns, with a resolving power varying from about 20 at the short end to about 100 at the long end, and a time resolution of 8 msec that yields milli-arcsecond angular resolution. The authors compare these data with two calibration stars, IRC+00233 (M7) and HD 155292 (K2), which have no detectable circumstellar dust, to characterize the limitations of the observation and analysis process. The occultation fringes of AFGL 5440 cannot be fit by any single-size model, indicating that the observed signal is a combination of the central star and a circumstellar dust shell produced by stellar mass loss. The authors therefore use the DUSTY radiative transfer code to model a circumstellar shell and fit both the observed occultation light curves and the spectral energy distribution (SED) from the literature. The best-fitting models yield a strong constraint on the inner radius of the dust shell, with a maximum dust temperature of Tmax = 950 K +/- 50 K, and an optical depth at 5 microns of 0.5 +/- 0.1. The observations are best fit by models with a density gradient of rho proportional to r^-2, or the gradient derived by Ivezi'c & Elitzur for a radiatively driven hydrodynamic outflow. The derived dust mass-loss rate is 6.5 x 10^-8 solar masses per year. However, the models cannot fit the observed IRAS 60-micron flux without assuming a substantial abundance of graphite or a substantially higher mass-loss rate in the past. This work represents the first modeling of this star over the entire infrared wavelength region and separately resolves the stellar photosphere and the inner edge of the circumstellar dust shell.",

draft_summary.title: Multi-spectral Observations of Lunar Occultations: I. Resolving The Dust Shell Around AFGL 5440
draft_summary.authors: Paul M. Harvey and Andrew Oldag
draft_summary.field_subfield: Astrophysics: circumstellar mass loss and dust shells around AGB stars
draft_summary.type_of_paper: Observational + modeling study of a lunar occultation of a carbon-rich AGB star
draft_summary.executive_summary: This paper presents high-speed, multi-wavelength observations of a lunar occultation of the dust-enshrouded carbon star AFGL 5440 (also known as OH 06.86-1.5 and IRAS 18036-2344), obtained on 28 Aug 2001 with the pMIRAS spectrophotometer on the McDonald Observatory 2.7-m telescope. The observations span a continuous wavelength range of 1-4 microns, with a resolving power varying from about 20 at the short end to about 100 at the long end, and a time resolution of 8 msec that yields milli-arcsecond angular resolution. The authors compare these data with two calibration stars, IRC+00233 (M7) and HD 155292 (K2), which have no detectable circumstellar dust, to characterize the limitations of the observation and analysis process. The occultation fringes of AFGL 5440 cannot be fit by any single-size model, indicating that the observed signal is a combination of the central star and a circumstellar dust shell produced by stellar mass loss. The authors therefore use the DUSTY radiative transfer code to model a circumstellar shell and fit both the observed occultation light curves and the spectral energy distribution (SED) from the literature. The best-fitting models yield a strong constraint on the inner radius of the dust shell, with a maximum dust temperature of Tmax = 950 K +/- 50 K, and an optical depth at 5 microns of 0.5 +/- 0.1. The observations are best fit by models with a density gradient of rho proportional to r^-2, or the gradient derived by Ivezi'c & Elitzur for a radiatively driven hydrodynamic outflow. The derived dust mass-loss rate is 6.5 x 10^-8 solar masses per year. However, the models cannot fit the observed IRAS 60-micron flux without assuming a substantial abundance of graphite or a substantially higher mass-loss rate in the past. This work represents the first modeling of this star over the entire infrared wavelength region and separately resolves the stellar photosphere and the inner edge of the circumstellar dust shell.
